expected_mode_rationale: collection transform over a slice — Light excludes slice/map transforms; no Strict risk trigger
_hypotheses: One entry per declared hypothesis, carrying everything the grader needs to decide whether it is really covered: the wording it must be described with, the test case that must have RUN (not skipped), the mutation that case must kill, and `contract_evidence` — a regex that must match sut.go, so a hypothesis cannot assert a behaviour the code under test never promised. These previously lived in three parallel lists (hypothesis_keywords / required_case_patterns / mutation) which could disagree — and did: H2 had an input scenario and no mutation, so the behaviour it promised was never verified.

hypotheses.description: off-by-one in the range bound drops the last element
nil/empty input yields an empty but NON-NIL result (JSON [] not null)

_allow_skipped_cases: This target is a pure function with no environment dependency, so no case has a legitimate reason to skip. A skipped case is discovered, not verified.
_json_field_types: Declared fields AND their JSON types. This is the single list: presence is required and the type is checked, so a wrong type can never silently disable a consistency rule. Note `int` rejects `true` (bool is an int subclass in Python).
_report_patterns: Markers the report must contain. The kill verification is mandatory; an assertion-necessity claim is NOT, because it is a different claim about a different thing (see references/killer-case-patterns.md).
